backup.title: Backup
backup.hint: Parts, photos and settings in one .tar file. Keep it on your computer or in the cloud.
backup.restoreHint: Replaces all parts with those in the backup and adds its photos. The current database is kept, so a restore can be undone.
backup.restoreSettings: Also restore the settings, from a full backup or an SD card copy (the device restarts)
backup.noSettings: This file has no settings (only the database), so they were kept.

deleteDb.confirmText: All parts ({n}) will be deleted from the board, with their quantities, bins and notes. Download a backup first if you may need them again.
deleteDb.confirmKeep: Until the next restore or delete, the board keeps one copy of the deleted database, which can be downloaded on this page. Photos stay until unused photos are removed.

csv.hint: Edit the parts in Excel, LibreOffice or Google Sheets, then import the file again.
csv.pickHint: Choose the separator. Excel in most European languages expects a semicolon.

system.notBack: The device has not come back. Check its power and Wi-Fi.
hw.layout.progressive: Every row from the same side
hw.fadeHint: How long every change takes to blend in, on the grid and on all work lights: switching on and off, brightness, colors and effects.
hw.whiteHint: Current per pixel is what one pixel draws at full white; empty uses the LED type's typical figure. To measure it, run the full white test, read the current at the supply and divide it by the number of pixels.
hw.whiteConfirm: Light all {n} pixels at full white for 2 minutes, past the brightness and the current limit? By the saved settings that is up to {a} A: make sure the power supply can deliver it.
hw.rgbGroup: W1, W2 and W3 drive one analog RGB strip
hw.micPsram: The microphone and the music effects need a board with PSRAM. On this board they are off, which leaves the memory to the web server.
hw.motionHint: A master switch over the lights: when nobody has been at the bench for a while, the work lights and the grid's effect fade to dark, and when someone stays, they come back as they were. Which lights are on, and their settings, never change. Wire the sensor's output to the analog microphone pin (GPIO35 by default, set in Microphone and pins). An LD2410C radar also notices someone sitting still; a PIR module (HC-SR501, AM312) only notices movement.
hw.motionDelays: The sensor has to see someone for the whole on delay, so passing by doesn't bring the lights back. Switching a light or an effect on from a page counts as being there.
hw.motionMic: The analog microphone uses the same pin. Saving switches the microphone to none.
hw.pinsHint: GPIO for each function. Each list offers only the pins the board can use for that function.
hw.pinsWarn: If the board stops responding after a pin change, hold its BOOT button for 10s: that restores all settings, including the default pins.
hw.errSize: Columns and rows must be between 1 and {max}.
hw.errSplit: Rows on line A must be between 1 and {max}.
